Setup: the opponent's creatures are Winding Constrictor 7/8, Verdurous Gearhulk 9/9, Rishkar 4/4 and Tireless Tracker 5/4. Winding Constrictor makes every -1/-1 counter placed on their creatures count double. So each Archfiend of Ifnir trigger puts two -1/-1 counters on each of their creatures.

1. Cast Brilliant Spectrum precombat. Pay U with an Island, B with a Swamp, and the generic with two more Islands. Two colors are spent, so you draw 2 Swamps. Then discard the 2 Swamps.
   - This is 2 discards, so Archfiend and Vizier each trigger twice.
   - Each opposing creature gets 4 -1/-1 counters, and Rishkar and Tireless Tracker die.
   - Shadowstorm Vizier is 3/5.
2. Cycle Horror of the Broken Lands for {B}, using a Swamp. This is the third trigger.
   - Each opposing creature has 6 counters.
   - Vizier is 4/6.
3. Cycle Floodwaters for {2}, using an Island and a Swamp. This is the fourth trigger.
   - Winding Constrictor has 8 counters and dies.
   - Verdurous Gearhulk has 8 counters, leaving it at toughness 1.
   - Vizier is 5/7.
4. Activate Stromkirk Condemned, discarding Elder Deep-Fiend. This is the fifth trigger.
   - Vizier is 6/8.
   - Gearhulk gets one more counter. The Constrictor is already dead, so the doubling no longer applies, and Gearhulk dies.
   - The opponent now has no creatures.
   - Stromkirk gets +1/+1 from its own ability and becomes 3/3.
5. Attack with Archfiend (5), Vizier (6) and Stromkirk (3). There are no blockers, so that is 14 damage, exactly lethal.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
I'm taking stock of my hand and lands, and sizing up the opponent's buffed-up creatures like the Winding Constrictor and Verdurous Gearhulk, both pumped well beyond their base stats with counters.

With the opponent at 14 life and lacking flying or reach, I'm figuring my evasive flying damage from Archfiend and Vizier of the Menagerie, boosted through repeated discards, could be the path to victory. Each discard also shrinks their board via -1/-1 counters, doubled by Winding Constrictor's trigger, which could help clear blockers or just race through the air.

I'm mapping out mana: seven lands, with cycling Archfiend's Horror side for B and Floodwaters for 2 generic, plus Stromkirk's free discard, all stacking triggers on Vizier and the counters effect. Casting Brilliant Spectrum for card draw and a two-card discard looks like a strong way to chain even more triggers in one turn.

Totaling it up: discarding the drawn swamps to Spectrum, then cycling Horror and Floodwaters, then using Stromkirk to discard the extra creature, gets five triggers total, pumping Vizier to 6/8.

Five -1/-1 triggers put 10 counters across the opponent's creatures, killing Rishkar, Tracker, Constrictor, and even the Gearhulk once toughness is exceeded. With the board clear, attacking with Vizier (6), Archfiend (5), and a pumped Stromkirk (3) adds up to exactly 14 damage.

But I need to double-check the Constrictor interaction — since it doubles the counters while alive, once it dies after its fourth trigger the doubling stops, meaning the Gearhulk only gets a single counter on the fifth trigger instead of two, leaving it with 9 counters total and just barely short of lethal toughness.

Mana works out to 7: 4+1+2. I need to discard two cards for Spectrum, so I'll use the swamps and keep Horror, Fiend, and Floodwaters flexible. I just need to make sure the remaining lands cover both U and B for casting Horror afterward.

With four Islands and three Swamps, Spectrum takes Island, Swamp, Island, Island, leaving Island, Swamp, Swamp for cycling Horror (B) and Floodwaters (two mana). Attacking with all three creatures after setting Stromkirk's pump precombat gets me exactly 14 damage, and Vizier's trigger fires five times across the discards and cycles.
